How do you get out of a rut? How do you know what your passion is? How do you realise what you were born to do?
Stuck in a rat race. How do I get out?

What do you hate the most about how things are in this world? I mean passionately "FUCK YOU!" hate. Are you aware of what you're good at? Can you use what you're good at to fix what you hate about the world? If not, can you branch some newer abilities from that to something relevant and useful to your passionate hatred? And, very importantly, can you do so without hurting anyone?
Try new things. Say yes to every opportunity that presents itself.

You won't know until you try new things. Assuming, of course, that you have the resources to be able to. Check out your local meetup. There are so many things to try. Metal detecting. Scuba diving. Snow Skiing. Wood working. Metal working. Shooting.

But if you are trying to make a career out of such things, don't sweat it. Most people do what they have to do to pay the bills. Passions are what you get to do on your own time. Most people work at jobs they hate.

I was of the same opinion. But it's so difficult when people around you have found their passion and are working 80-100 hours per week out of pure passion and not compulsion. It just makes you think if this is where you wanted to end up. I have a lot of things going on in the side and I love them all. Solely for the reason that I can do them at my will. There is no pressure or compulsion to be good at it. I don't want to ruin those hobbies for myself by taking them too seriously. Hence, my conundrum.
I have seen many times where making a hobby a business takes the fun out of the hobby. Often times it implodes.

Personally, I've been dealing inner conflict with clinical depression since I was 7 on top of the rat race.

So one day, I tried out something new. I got into different kinds of meditation for a few months and I just finished reading a book of The Power of Now.

I reccomend you try meditation before reading it but I found the book to really help if your life situation sucks atm and you don't have to remain dependent on the world around you to have inner peace.
Thanks. It's going on my wishlist now! I have practiced yoga since childhood. Helps me keep at peace in front of others. But inner peace, different ballgame altogether.
I would need more specifics. Hard to give blanket advice. Are you stuck in a job you don't like? What do you currently do? Why are you still doing it if you don't like it? What do you want to do?

I like my job. I like the field that I am in. The people that I work with are very understanding. I have a lot of freedom. However, I feel like I am not learning anything new of late. There are a lot of things to learn, but I'm not being given an opportunity to learn them practically. I can learn things on my own as well, but it's just theoretical. I don't want to do that. And since I have been in the job for a long time, they have started to take me for granted. I am not a "flight-risk" in their eyes. Also, the job that I am at is the best that I can get in my field with the degree that I hold and the place that I am in. So, it's comfortable and convenient. It's very difficult if you "settle down" so early in life. I still continue to do it because it pays my bills and lets me do whatever I want when I'm out of office. I want to be passionate about something, anything really. I have tried tens of hobbies, but I'm zealous at the beginning and eventually I lose interest.

What about asking if you can take a class or get more training? Or maybe ask for more/different work? Unless you tell them how you feel, they might not change anything.

If you've been there a while and are a good worker, there will always be other options. Sure, maybe it's a great job, but it's not the only job for you. Don't think that you're stuck there.

I have no answers for you. I just want you to know that I'm struggling with the same thing. My job here, aside from a yearly bump in pay, has pretty much plateaued. Knocking on 30, and I still don't know what I want to be when I "grow up." This can't be all there is. I don't really have passions or hobbies - at least none that I can harness to put toward a career of any kind.

I also understand that a lot of what's holding me back is anxiety, a general dislike for change, and my own unwillingness to step outside of my comfort zone.

What I mean to say is, have you recognized your own flaws in a way that you can understand, at the very least, what's holding you back?

When I was in college I was a starry eyed super liberal kid ignorant of the world around me. I thought things like "I will never work at a desk job", "money is not happiness" and most of all "I would never compromise my beliefs for a job", well I have done all of things over the past few years and have reaped the benefits and downfalls of those actions. I made a lot of money from a very good desk job wherein I sell my soul daily for the almighty dollar. I have commoditized myself, and apparently I was marketable, and for a long time I took solace in the fact that although I was miserable I was making good money and was very comfortable.

But after these last few years I am fucking sick of it, sick of what I do and sick of the person that I have become. So my wife and I (who is the real bread winner in the family) have decided that enough is enough.

We are currently in the process of selling pretty much everything we own, and getting ready to move when my contracts and visa expire this coming fall. We will go somewhere south, warm and close to the ocean like the places that we grew up in. We will work jobs at which we don't make any money really (teaching, NGO's) but that will allow us more time with each other and to exist with significantly less stress. We will get rid of all of the BS in our lives, get back to basics and work to find happiness, individual happiness, happiness in our relationship, and happiness in life.

We are doing this to get out of our rut. We both know what we are passionate about (her, working with animals; me, working with children) and we will follow those passions wherever they lead regardless of the money or lack thereof.

This is how we will discover our true selves and come to know happiness, by leaving the 9 to 5 rat race behind, leaving all of the stress that comes with the chase for money behind, and doing work that we can be proud of; work that will immediately benefit this world to make it a better place, work that will fulfill us, work that by making others happy will make us happy.

Just do what makes you happy, that is almost all there is to it. If your lucky, eventually you will become a master and the money will follow, and if not, you will still be doing something that makes you happy.

A fancy apartment filled with nice things, bank accounts, credit cards, debts, none of these things will ever make you happy nor will they truly work to define who you are as a person.
